Maya (Support): @Will thanks for the report — I see you raised this to support. Can you paste the exact request you sent (headers redacted) and the error the indexer returned?
Will (Customer): sure — repro below. We switched to an int8 quantized profile to cut cost and suddenly our vector store complains about dimension mismatch when ingesting new embeddings. Old embeddings were 768, new ones are 384. No schema changes on our side.

Will (Customer): ```python
# simplified client
resp = client.embeddings.create(
    model='rwdw/embedding-latest',
    inputs=["some text"] * 16,
    precision='int8',
    batch_size=16
)
print(len(resp.data[0].embedding))  # -> 384
```

Will (Customer): indexer error: "Vector dimension 384 incompatible with collection dimension 768"

Maya (Support): thanks. Two quick asks: 1) which exact model alias/version is that (`rwdw/embedding-latest` can point to different variants), and 2) can you share request_id from the response headers (like `x-rwdw-request-id`)?

Will (Customer): alias is `rwdw/embedding-latest` — id: `req_01GXYZ123` (masked).

Jin (ML Eng): quick high level: quantization (fp16/int8) should not change embedding dimensionality. If dims changed it's usually because the alias pointed to a different model family (e.g., a compressed 384-dim embedder) or client code is accidentally reshaping/truncating. Two places to check: the model metadata for the alias and the client-side post-processing.

Sam (Infra): @Jin I'll pull model resolution for that alias now.

Sam (Infra): ```
# server-side lookup
GET /models/aliases/rwdw/embedding-latest
-> {"resolved_model": "rwdw/embedding-384-int8-v2", "created_by": "ops/scripts/alias_sync"}
```

Jin (ML Eng): there you go — alias resolves to a 384-dim variant. That's the root cause. The quantized variant you were bumped to is a smaller embedding model (different architecture/config), not the full 768-dim model quantized.

Will (Customer): oh wow — but we explicitly passed `precision='int8'`. We didn't intend to change dims. How did the alias get changed?

Maya (Support): looks like an automated alias sync script rotated some aliases to lower-cost variants for canary testing last week (ops note: `alias_sync`), but we should never swap dims silently. That's a bug in our aliasing policy. Apologies.

Jin (ML Eng): for immediate repro/rollback options:
- Option A: use the canonical model name that guarantees dims, e.g., `rwdw/embedding-768-fp16` or `rwdw/embedding-768-int8` (if we have an int8 quantized 768 model) — avoid using `-latest` alias.
- Option B: update your index collection to accept 384-dim embeddings (if you want the smaller model long-term).

Jin (ML Eng): to list available model metadata you can run:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/models | jq '.models[] | {name:.name, dims:.metadata.embedding_dim, precision:.metadata.precision}'
```

Will (Customer): ran that - I see both `embedding-768-int8` and `embedding-384-int8`. The alias was pointing at the 384 one. Customer-side we assumed alias kept dims. Our ingestion pipeline flattens single embeddings to 1D arrays and throws errors when shape mismatches, so we need to either pick the right model or reindex.

Maya (Support): for throughput/latency notes: int8 variants are expected to be faster/more throughput, but the behavior of batching can change tail latency. We recommend starting with `batch_size=8` and `max_wait_ms=50` for production; monitor `tokens_per_sec` in Console.

Jin (ML Eng): further debugging tip — if you see odd half-sized vectors in client code, also check for dtype casts + memory views. Example bug we've seen:
```
# bad: treat bytes as float16 array then view as float32 -> halves length
buf = np.frombuffer(resp_bytes, dtype=np.float16).view(np.float32)
```
But in this case alias resolution explains it.

Sam (Infra): I rolled back the alias to the 768-dim family and created an internal incident to stop alias sync from rotating embedding dims automatically. ID INC-2026.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026/03/15 15:32 UTC - alias_sync disable flag set, infra patch rolled to prod :white_check_mark: 

Will (Customer): confirming on our side — switched to `rwdw/embedding-768-int8` explicitly and re-ingested. All good, indexing succeeded. Latency slightly better with int8. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Maya (Support): great — action items: 1) we'll add a console warning when alias changes embedding_dim, 2) we fixed alias_sync to avoid dim-changing rotations and added a test to prevent silent swaps, 3) docs update: call out that quantization does not imply dimensionality changes and to prefer explicit model names for stable schemas.

Jin (ML Eng): TL;DR: quantization shouldn't change dims — different model variants do. When troubleshooting: check alias resolution, model metadata `.metadata.embedding_dim`, and client-side reshape/bytes handling.

Will (Customer): thanks everyone! saved our ingest job. :rocket:
